gloss: naive; unworldly; inexperienced in the ways of the world

definitions.gloss: naive; unworldly; inexperienced in the ways of the world
definitions.explanation: A person who lacks knowledge of social norms, common sense, or how society works, often due to a sheltered upbringing.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}は{世間知|せけんし}らずだ。
examples.english: That person is naive about the ways of the world.

examples.japanese: {世間知|せけんし}らずと{言|い}われても{仕方|しかた}がない。
examples.english: It can't be helped if people call you naive.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いころは{世間知|せけんし}らずで、いろいろ{失敗|しっぱい}した。
examples.english: When I was young, I was naive about the world and made many mistakes.

notes:
Combines {世間|せけん} (the world, society) with {知|し}らず (not knowing). Functions both as a noun describing such a person and as a na-adjective-like descriptor. Carries a mildly critical tone, implying someone is out of touch with reality or social expectations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {世間知|せけんし}らずな{人|ひと}: a naive person
- {世間知|せけんし}らずだと{思|おも}われる: to be seen as unworldly
- {世間知|せけんし}らずのお{嬢|じょう}さん: a sheltered young lady

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {箱入|はこい}り{娘|むすめ}: sheltered daughter — specifically refers to a young woman raised in a protective environment, while {世間知|せけんし}らず applies to anyone regardless of gender
- {青二才|あおにさい}: greenhorn — implies youthful inexperience with a more dismissive tone, while {世間知|せけんし}らず focuses on lack of social awareness
